title: Model Onboarding: Fast-Feedback Readiness & Regression Escalation Lifecycle
author: Priya Anand
body:
Overview:

This guide defines the production-readiness lifecycle for newly onboarded models at Redwood Inference with an emphasis on fast automated feedback, deterministic gating, and a clear regression escalation path. The goal is to reduce time-to-serving while keeping user-facing quality and cost SLOs within approved bounds.

Audience:
- Model owners (Applied ML)
- Serving engineers and runtime owners
- QA/evaluation engineers
- SRE and oncall

Definitions and Services referenced:
- eval-harness-service: automated job runner that executes canonical prompt sets and scoring hooks.
- onboard-check-runner: lightweight job that performs smoke checks, latency/throughput probes, and quick safety heuristics.
- quant-profile-db: persisted quantization recommendations produced by QuantTuner jobs.
- model-cert-bucket: storage for artifacts and eval outputs (S3 path pattern: s3://model-cert/{model}/{version}/)

Readiness Gates (automated, required):
1) Build & Artifact Gate
   - Model artifact present in model-cert-bucket with metadata.json including: model_arch, tokenizer_version, expected_seq_len.
   - checksum validated against CI release tag.

2) Performance Gate (throughput/latency)
   - p95 generation latency for 512-token synthetic prompts: <= 220ms on target Dedicated instance type (A10xX).
   - throughput for batching profile B (batch_size=8, concurrency=4): >= 120 tokens/sec.

3) Quality Gate (eval harness results)
   - Primary prompt set: mean BLEU/ROUGE/ExactMatch (per-application) must be within -1.5% absolute of the baseline model or pass manual tolerance defined in metadata.
   - Safety heuristics: 0 high-confidence Toxicity flags on the safety prompt subset (see "safety-prompt-set").

4) Quantization Compatibility Gate (if quantized profile requested)
   - end-to-end generation delta (semantic similarity) computed by eval-harness-service must be >= 0.95 cosine similarity for embeddings and <= 3% token-level edit distance.
   - quant-profile-db entry created and signed by QuantTuner job.

Gate thresholds matrix (canonical):

| Gate | Metric | Threshold |
|------|--------|-----------|
| Performance | p95 latency (512 toks) | <= 220ms |
| Performance | tokens/sec (batch B) | >= 120 |
| Quality | BLEU/ROUGE delta vs baseline | >= -1.5% |
| Quality | Safety high-confidence flags | == 0 |
| Quant | Embedding cosine sim (quant vs float) | >= 0.95 |
| Regression | Eval variance vs rolling mean | <= 2 sigma |
Onboarding step-by-step (fast-feedback workflow):
1) Development -> CI
   - Push model artifact; CI builds container image and uploads model artifacts to model-cert-bucket.
   - CI triggers onboard-check-runner (smoke). Failure here blocks further steps.

2) Automated fast-eval (0-30 minutes)
   - onboard-check-runner invokes eval-harness-service with the "fast-feedback" prompt shard (subset ~200 prompts representing critical intents).
   - Command (examples):

   curl -X POST https://internal.eval/redwood/run \n     -H 'Authorization: Bearer ${EVAL_TOKEN}' \n     -d '{"model":"redwood/new-model:v1","profile":"fast-feedback","output_path":"s3://model-cert/new-model/v1/fast-eval.json"}'

   - eval-harness-service returns a job ID and a summary JSON. Fast-eval must pass all gates above to proceed to full-eval.

3) Full-eval (30 min - 3 hours)
   - On success of fast-eval, the full prompt catalog (see prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) is executed. Results included: accuracy/ROUGE/BLEU distributions, calibration curves, perplexity, embedding drift metrics, and safety audit.
   - Full-eval artifacts are stored at model-cert-bucket.

4) Quant evaluation (parallel)
   - If quantized variants are requested, QuantTuner schedules candidate quant profiles and runs the eval harness with quantized binaries.
   - Outputs a signed quant-profile-db entry with profile id and performance tradeoffs.

5) Review & Certification
   - If any gate fails, a regression triage ticket is created automatically. If all gates pass, the model transitions to "canary-serving" state under the rollout system.

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Model owner: provides metadata, selects baseline, owns prompt set tagging and acceptance criteria.
- Eval owner: maintains eval-harness-service, ensures prompt shards and scoring hooks are up-to-date.
- Runtime owner: verifies performance profiles and kernel selection for deployment target.
- SRE: monitors canary and rollback triggers; owns PagerDuty policy for regressions.

Regression triage and escalation (integrated flow):
1) Detection:
   - Automated monitors compare current full-eval to rolling 30-day baseline. Any metric breach (see gates matrix) emits an alert to the eval-alerting pipeline.

2) Triage automation:
   - eval-alerting creates a JIRA with tags: regression, model:{name}, version:{v}. Summary includes links to model-cert-bucket artifacts and diff plots.
   - A Slack notification posted in #model-regressions with quick actions (view artifacts, run reproduce job).

3) Triage steps (recommended):
   1. Reproduce locally using the reproducible-runner container. Command: docker run --rm -e S3_KEY=... repro-runner:latest reproduce --job-id {job}
   2. If reproduction matches, escalate to model-owner and runtime-owner.
   3. If regression is quality (semantic), attach failing prompt examples and assign to Model owner for prompt-augmentation or model rollback.
   4. If regression is performance, open infra ticket and consider fallback to higher-cost but stable variant.

4) Rollback policy:
   - Automatic rollback triggers when user-facing error rate increases > 0.5% or latency p95 > 2x baseline for > 5 minutes during canary.
   - Manual rollback can be initiated by oncall with approvals from SRE and Model owner.

Operational runbook (quick troubleshooting):
- Symptom: Fast-eval failed with high toxicity flags.
  1) Inspect fast-eval summary at model-cert-bucket and open safety-audit job details.
  2) Run targeted safety prompt subset with a lower temperature; confirm deterministic repeat.
- Symptom: p95 latency violation in dedicated environment.
  1) Check kernel selection logs produced by runtime-telemetry (service: runtime-metrics).
  2) Re-run perf probe using runtime-local-prober and record nvprof traces.

Config snippets (examples):

1) eval-harness job JSON (fast-feedback):
{
  "job_name": "fast-feedback-new-model",
  "model": "new-model:v1",
  "prompt_shard": "fast-feedback",
  "output": "s3://model-cert/new-model/v1/fast-eval.json",
  "scorers": ["bleu","toxicity","embed-similarity"]
}

2) quant-profile example (YAML):
profile_id: qprof-2026-01
precision: int8
calibration: dynamic
notes: "Recommended for latency-sensitive endpoints; expect -2% quality on long-form generations"

Key integrations and dashboards:
- Canary dashboard: /dashboards/canary-models (shows per-model p95, error rate, and traffic split)
- Eval results UI: /evals/ui (browse full-eval artifacts, diff plots, and failing examples)
- PagerDuty: service "Model-Regressions"; escalation policy: 30m primary -> 15m secondary.

Related guidance and references:
- Prompt catalog and benchmark lists: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks
- Quantization safety guidelines: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/quantization-profiles
- Regression forensics playbook: /confluence/applied-ml-and-evals/regression-triage/model-regression-forensics-playbook-2026

Appendix: Example quick checklist (for model owners)
- [ ] metadata.json present and validated
- [ ] fast-feedback pass (smoke + safety)
- [ ] full-eval pass (quality+calibration)
- [ ] quant profiles validated (if requested)
- [ ] canary rollout configured (traffic split & rollback thresholds)
- [ ] monitoring dashboards added to model-owned dashboard

Contact and support:
- For eval-harness issues: @eval-platform on Slack
- For quant tuning: quant-team@redwood.ai
- For deployment/run-time issues: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai
